rationale: The workflow runs a 3x Python-version matrix on ubuntu-latest and installs heavy Python dependencies (torch, opencv, etc. from requirements.txt) from scratch in every job, with pip's cache disabled via --no-cache-dir and no actions/cache step. Evidence (P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE measured experiment and P-LIT-GHA-CACHE dependency-cache pattern) supports caching pip dependencies to reduce CI time. I added an actions/cache@v4 step for ~/.cache/pip after setup-python and before installs, keyed on runner OS, matrix python-version, and the dependency files (pyproject.toml + requirements.txt, since pyproject.toml declares dependencies dynamically from requirements.txt). I removed --no-cache-dir from the pip install commands so pip can read/write the restored cache. All checkout, system-dependency, build, and test steps are preserved unchanged, so build/test coverage is intact and no permissions, secrets, deployment, or new network access is introduced.
